families.reason: Publish the independently verified narrow occupier-side lease-administration boundary provisionally; retain classification, economics, acquisition and other research gaps without eligibility or investment-score claims. Unresolved product and candidate dispositions remain recorded in the workflow and closure.

family_lineage.analysis_summary: The frozen NAICS definition places 531390 in residual real-estate-related services while explicitly excluding lessors, real-estate agents and brokers, property managers, and appraisers. Frozen supplemental excerpts describe recurring occupier-side lease-administration work, including lease-data maintenance, date monitoring, charge validation, reconciliation, and reporting. This supports only a provisional operating-boundary hypothesis for occupier-side commercial lease administration; it does not establish market economics, acquisition availability, workforce characteristics, or that every listed collection activity belongs within the boundary. The three required NAPCS identities and the prior Deposit brokerage candidate remain unresolved because their labels identify brokerage or title-insurance services rather than demonstrating the proposed lease-administration boundary.

candidate_dispositions.rationale: The frozen candidate card identifies this prior seed as Deposit brokerage and records retrieved collisions with land-sale and land-rental brokerage identities. It provides no evidence that the candidate is an occupier-side commercial lease-administration service or that it belongs in the provisional proposal.

identity_dispositions.rationale: NAICS 531390 is a residual category for real-estate-related services, excluding lessors, agents and brokers, property managers, and appraisers. The frozen lease-administration excerpts describe recurring lease records, dates, charge validation, reconciliations, and reporting, supporting a tentative service boundary. The sources do not directly state that this operating market belongs to NAICS 531390, so the mapping is provisional.

The required identity is labeled agent and brokerage services for sale of nonresidential real estate. Its frozen identity and relationship records establish a product label and association, but do not establish that it is the same operating service as occupier-side lease administration. The NAICS residual definition also expressly excludes real-estate agents and brokers, so no mapping is supported on the supplied evidence.

The required identity is labeled agent and brokerage services for sale and rental of land. The frozen records identify a product category, not its buyer, delivery model, or equivalence to commercial lease administration. No affirmative family-local non-mapping is established, but no supported mapping is available.

The required identity is titled title insurance policy underwriting services. The frozen materials identify it as a product category but do not establish buyer, delivery, regulatory responsibility, or overlap with the proposed occupier-side lease-administration service. The NAICS cross-reference separately identifies title-insurance underwriting as classified in insurance activities, but the record set does not justify a final local disposition beyond unresolved.

proposed_markets.boundary: A provisional boundary for recurring, occupier-side administration of commercial real-estate lease records and obligations: maintaining lease and portfolio data, monitoring critical dates, validating charges, reconciling recurring lease information, and producing agreed reporting. It is limited to administrative service delivery for occupier clients and does not include acting as a property manager, real-estate agent or broker, appraiser, lessor, title insurer, legal adviser, or a provider assuming unverified client-fund custody or payment-enforcement responsibility.
proposed_markets.definition: A recurring business service in which a provider administers commercial occupiers' lease records, recurring lease events, charge-validation and reconciliation workflows, and periodic reporting.

acquisition_universe.statement: The frozen materials do not establish an independent acquisition universe, business population, ownership profile, transaction availability, or eligibility for this proposed service boundary.

ambient_ai_workflow.statement: AI-assisted review may be an emerging workflow feature because one retained provider excerpt refers to senior review of AI-generated findings, but the materials do not establish routine adoption, productivity effects, or autonomous delivery.

buyer.statement: The buyer is provisionally limited to commercial real-estate occupiers or their corporate real-estate functions; one retained provider excerpt states that its lease-administration service is offered only to occupiers.

delivery.statement: Delivery appears to be a recurring administrative workflow involving portfolio and database maintenance, lease-event updates, date monitoring, charge validation, reconciliation, and monthly reporting.

economics_risk.statement: Advertised delivery models include per-location, per-transaction, resource-based, and performance-driven structures, but the frozen materials do not establish margins, contract duration, demand magnitude, payment risk, or operating performance.

job.statement: Maintain current lease and portfolio records, monitor dates and lease events, validate charges, reconcile recurring information, and provide periodic reports for occupier stakeholders.

workforce.statement: The frozen material identifies commercial lease administration as a workload area but does not establish required credentials, labor availability, staffing model, employee versus contractor mix, or labor exposure.

explicit_exclusions: Residential or nonresidential real-estate brokerage and agency services.
Acting as a lessor or leasing property on the provider's own account.
Title-insurance underwriting or title-insurance agency activity.
Legal advice, title search, or title settlement services.
Rent, common-area, or payment-obligation collection work where buyer, payer/payee role, client-fund custody, authorization, and contractual risk allocation have not been established.
